title: Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: He was Rabbi Yochanan’s student, as in [Berakhot 38b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.38b.9-10): Rabbi Zeira wondered at it: “What has Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet to do with Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba? … Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet was not precise; he did not review.” Hyman infers from this that he was Rabbi Yochanan’s student, although not a distinguished student like Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba.

In [Shabbat 53a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.53a.8) and [Ketubot 77a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.77a.15): when Rabbi Zeira arrived in the Land of Israel, he found Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet teaching in Rabbi Yochanan’s name. Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet also speaks in Rabbi Yochanan’s name, as in [Pesachim 54a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.54a.1), [Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 2:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Pesachim.2.5.4) and Tanchuma, Lekh Lekha 10; [Bereshit Rabbah 43:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.43.3) reads “in the name of Rabbi Yonatan,” and Hyman proposes Rabbi Yochanan. In [Berakhot 33a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.33a.31), Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet reports that Rabbi Yose [son of Rabbi Chanina] asked Rabbi Yochanan a question in Sidon.[^3]

He likewise speaks in Rabbi Elazar’s name, as in [Taanit 29b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.29b.5), [Yoma 29a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.29a.6), [Megillah 16b](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.16b.4-7), [Sanhedrin 7a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.7a.3), [Shevuot 18b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shevuot.18b.11) and [Chullin 50b:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.50b.8). Hyman cites the Rosh’s reading for the passages on 50b and [Chullin 52b:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.52b.11).[^4] In [Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 1:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sanhedrin.1.1.13): Rabbi Ba and Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet had a lawsuit and came to Rabbi Yitzchak, who ruled in favor of Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet.

notes.text: Saved Davidson Taanit29b fully writes Rabbi Elazar for the cited Binyamin teaching. This supports the contextual expansion instead of a mechanical resh-aleph rule. Pesachim2:5 is Jerusalem Talmud, and the Yose/Yonatan/Assi corrections remain Hyman’s. The supplied לא דיין is read in the precise-reviewing sense indicated by the adjoining לא מהדר.

The inspected Berakhot 38b directly contrasts Chiyya bar Abba’s precision and repeated study with Binyamin bar Yefet’s report in Yochanan’s name. This is the basis of Hyman’s student-status inference, not a new authority relation. His Yonatan-to-Yochanan proposal, bracketed Yose patronymic and exact Rosh readings remain occurrence-specific and attributed.

[Berakhot 33a:31](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.33a.31) also gives an alternate questioner, Rabbi Shimon ben Yaakov of Tyre, without inserting “son of Rabbi Chanina” after Yose. [Taanit 29b:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.29b.5) has Rabbi Binyamin citing Rabbi Elazar without a patronymic. [Seder HaDorot 761](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=761&lang=en) calls that attribution to bar Yefet a possibility. [Bereshit Rabbah 43:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.43.3) names Rabbi Yonatan, as Hyman reports.

The linked Bavli passages have Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet citing Rabbi Elazar at 50b and Rabbi Ela at 52b. In the consulted Vilna text of the Rosh, [Rosh on Chullin 3:33:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_on_Chullin.3.33.1) brackets “Rabbi Elazar said” for the first passage, while [Rosh on Chullin 3:40:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_on_Chullin.3.40.1) explicitly names Rabbi Elazar for the second.
